BeatScope measures a song; Beathi turns the measurements into a film. Everything runs on your machine.

**A model-backed path, measured on held-out material.** `--backend enhanced` (and a
high-precision button in the studio) takes beats from the Beat This model and keeps
BeatScope's onsets, energy, tempo and exports. It agrees with the official pipeline
element by element. On 999 GTZAN tracks - which the model was not trained on - it
scores 0.8909 Beat F1 and 0.7871 downbeat F1, against 0.9908 on Ballroom, which is
training data. That gap is the honest version of the earlier number.

**Two experiments that did not work, left off.** A second onset extractor scored
0.519 against the shipping extractor's 0.649 on a development split, with each
mechanism swept separately; a local timing refinement had no room on a corpus where
the model is already at 0.99. Both are recorded with their measurements rather than
tuned until they looked good.

**Honest bookkeeping.** Benchmark runs now state their denominators and cannot
reuse predictions made under a different configuration; projects say when a meter
or a tempo was assumed rather than measured; the runtime counts beats in the
project's own meter.

**Known limits.** Classical and piano material scores lower (0.66-0.63 across two
corpora); tempo changes cost continuity; the checkpoint's licence has not been
reviewed for redistribution.
